newsitem.title: FRANCE: Juppe urges French to assume wartime shame, glory.
newsitem.headline: Juppe urges French to assume wartime shame, glory.

text.p: Prime Minister Alain Juppe urged his countrymen on Wednesday to take on board the shame and the glory of France's wartime and collaborationist years, saying they should "look reality in the face".
Juppe was addressing an audience of young people who had watched Claude Berri's latest film "Lucie Aubrac", the tale of two Resistance fighters who fought the four-year Nazi occupation of France.
"It took almost 50 years before...President Jacques Chirac said 'we are all collectively responsible for our past"," the Gaullist Juppe said.
"I believe it is important that we look this reality in the face, that we accept the shame there is in all this, the glory, the heroism," he added.
Chirac had in July 1995 recognised the responsibility of the collaborationist Vichy regime in the persecution of Jews on French territory.

The film's release comes at a time when France is being forced to face its wartime past by the upcoming trial of former Vichy official Maurice Papon, accused of organising the deportation of 1,690 Jews from the southwestern Bordeaux region.

Papon was ordered to trial last month by a Supreme court after 16 years of legal procedure, delayed by successive French administrations reluctant to have a public trial dredge up embrassing revelations over France's wartime collaboration.
